sources.citation: Fatima, M., Kelso, C., Hai, F.I. (2026). Beyond the isotherm: Limits in prediction of PFAS breakthrough behaviour in continuous flow column. Journal of Water Process Engineering, 81, 109352.

evidence_chunks.text: Batch kinetic isotherm and continuous flow column experiments were performed for five per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). Coefficient of determination (R2) was higher for Pseudo-Second-Order (PSO, 0.92) than Pseudo-First-Order (PFO, 0.88) kinetic model.
Adsorption of PFAS on GAC is a function of chain length. AER consistently outperformed GAC for all PFAS. Efficiency gap between GAC and AER decreased with increasing PFAS chain length.
Isotherm predicted chain-length dependent trends as in continuous flow columns, but underpredicted the service life of the fixed bed continuous flow column.

source_limitations: Full article text not accessible due to publisher restrictions; only abstract and highlights inspected.
Study conditions (PFAS concentrations, EBCT, bed properties) must be obtained from full text beyond inspected snippet.
Uncertainty treatment and quantitative comparison between isotherm-based predictions and observed breakthrough are not fully visible in inspected content.

sources.citation: [Preprint] Authors not specified in snippet (2025). Which natural organic matter components limit PFAS removal by activated carbon. ChemRxiv preprint.

evidence_chunks.text: In this study, we conducted batch and column experiments with granular activated carbon (GAC) and different natural organic matter (NOM) fractions to identify the specific NOM components that inhibit the adsorption of short- and long-chain PFAS.

Adsorption of short-chain PFAS was significantly inhibited by the <3 kDa fraction obtained via ultrafiltration. This fraction, abundant in low molecular weight hydrophilic compounds, competes directly with short-chain PFAS for adsorption sites.
Long-chain PFAS adsorption was significantly reduced in the presence of the hydrophobic neutral (HON) fraction, isolated via resin fractionation.
In column experiments, competition from the HON fraction not only reduced long-chain PFAS adsorption but also that of short-chain PFAS, an effect not observed in batch experiments.

Modeling PFAS breakthrough behavior using the isotherm, kinetic, and column data showed that slower adsorption kinetics, rather than equilibrium adsorption capacity, predominantly control the breakthrough of long-chain PFAS.

source_limitations: Preprint not yet peer reviewed; methods and data may change before journal publication.
Exact column operating conditions (EBCT, bed depth, flow) and quantitative breakthrough times need to be extracted from full tables/figures beyond sampled lines.
Study uses a specific GAC and NOM fractions; translation to other carbons and natural waters may be limited.
sources.title: Which natural organic matter components limit PFAS removal by activated carbon?

sources.citation: Hopkins, Z.R., Knappe, D.R.U., et al. (2023). Sorptive removal of short-chain perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) during drinking water treatment using activated carbon and anion exchanger. Environmental Sciences Europe, 35, 46.

evidence_chunks.text: The granular carbon selection test (GCS test) was developed to compare the adsorption capacities of different types of GAC. Breakthrough curves for PFBA and PFOA using five different GAC types are shown.

GAC column tests were used to determine the operation time of a full-scale GAC adsorber. The GAC adsorber used in the pilot-scale test received contaminated groundwater and PFAS concentrations were measured at different bed depths of the adsorber.
PFBA breakthrough could be observed at 5,000 bed volumes (BV). At a specific throughput of 11,000 BV the effluent and initial concentration were equal.
A 10% breakthrough is observed at 6000 BV for PFBA, at 11,000 BV for PFPeA, at 16,000 BV for PFHxA, at 20,000 BV for PFHpA and at 23,000 BV for PFOA.

Under the given boundary conditions (especially the given initial concentrations for PFAS and a 10% breakthrough in maximum), GAC removal is effective for long-chain PFOA and short-chain PFHpA and PFHxA. However, GAC adsorption is not effective or results in short operation times for PFBA and PFPeA.

source_limitations: Lab-scale GAC selection tests and a single pilot adsorber may not represent all full-scale configurations.
Detailed batch isotherm or kinetic data are not emphasized; focus is on column and pilot behavior.
Mixture effects and competing constituents are specific to the studied groundwater and may differ in other matrices.
sources.title: Sorptive removal of short-chain perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) during drinking water treatment using activated carbon and anion exchanger

sources.citation: Tang, X., et al. (2026). Dissolved Organic Matter and Pretreatment Effects on PFAS Removal by Granular Activated Carbon. AWWA Water Science, 8(2), e70053.

evidence_chunks.text: In this study, we evaluated the impact of dissolved organic matter (DOM) concentration and pretreatment on GAC use rates for PFAS removal.

DOM pretreatment methods included three full-scale treatment processes—coagulation-flocculation-sedimentation (CFS), CFS followed by ozonation (CFS-O3), and CFS-O3 followed by biological activated carbon (CFS-O3-BAC)—as well as five bench-scale jar test pretreatments.

SPDFR_full-scale together with parameters of a pilot-scale GAC column were used as PSDM inputs to generate scaled-up PFAS breakthrough curves, which were used to predict bed volumes that can be treated until 10% or 50% breakthrough.

source_limitations: Only abstract and limited methods text accessible; full breakthrough curves and service-life predictions are in figures and tables not inspected.
Study focuses on DOM pretreatment and a specific utility water matrix; extrapolation to other waters requires caution.
Uncertainty analysis in scale-up from pilot to full-scale is not visible in inspected content.

sources.citation: Brusseau, M.L., et al. (2021). Column versus batch methods for measuring PFOS and PFOA sorption to geomedia. Environmental Pollution, 268(B), 115917.

evidence_chunks.text: The objective of this study is to compare the consistency between column and batch experiment methods for measuring solid-phase sorption coefficients and isotherms for per and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) are used as representative PFAS, and experiments are conducted with three natural porous media with differing geochemical properties.
PFAS adsorption isotherms determined from column and batch methods match very well. The isotherms are consistent for adsorption of PFOS and PFOA by three geomedia.
Retardation factors determined from column data with different methods are similar.

source_limitations: Study concerns geomedia sorption (soils/sediments), not engineered adsorbers for treatment, though methodological insights are transferable.
Continuous-flow experiments are laboratory columns, not pilot/full-scale treatment systems.
Breakthrough criteria, service life, and operational flow conditions for water treatment applications are not addressed.
sources.title: Column versus batch methods for measuring PFOS and PFOA sorption to geomedia

sources.citation: Pannu, M.W., Huang, A., Plumlee, M.H. (2024). Variable PFAS removal by adsorbent media with sufficient prediction of breakthrough despite reduced contact time at pilot scale. Water Environment Research, 96(5), e11035.

evidence_chunks.text: One alternative adsorbent (AA) and five ion exchange (IX) resins were tested for the removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from groundwater in pilot-scale columns for up to 19 months using empty bed contact times (EBCTs) representative of full-scale treatment.

For the six detected PFAS in the pilot feed water, the long-chain PFAS (perfluorooctanoic acid [PFOA], perfluorooctanesulfonic acid [PFOS], and perfluorohexanesulfonic acid [PFHxS]) were well removed with only PFOA eventually breaking through as the media became exhausted.

Perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS) was also well removed, whereas short-chain PFCAs (perfluoropentanoic acid [PFPeA] and perfluorobutanoic acid [PFBA]) were not removed (i.e., immediate breakthrough).
Other pilot-scale evaluations for PFAS treatment media may only be operated long enough to reach initial breakthrough of the target PFAS to identify longest-lasting media.

source_limitations: Only abstract and limited text inspected; detailed EBCTs, flow rates, bed depths, and breakthrough criteria are in full article.
Work focuses on IX resins and a specific alternative adsorbent rather than conventional GAC.
Translation from site-specific pilot conditions to other groundwater matrices may require additional validation.
sources.title: Variable PFAS removal by adsorbent media with sufficient prediction of breakthrough despite reduced contact time at pilot scale

Using the pore surface diffusion model (PSDM), intraparticle diffusivity was found to be proportional to (dp)0.25 when considering data up to about 70% PFAS breakthrough.

evidence_chunks.text: PFAS removal performance of granular activated carbon (GAC) and ion exchange resin (IX) was evaluated and compared using a segmented column system with full scale media under continuous flow conditions.

Despite the rapid breakthrough of short chain PFAS by GAC; ease of operation, low unit media cost, and consistent PFAS and co-contaminant adsorption has resulted in GAC being one of the most commonly implemented technologies for the treatment of PFAA contaminated groundwater.
Long-term column tests are needed to generate PFAS treatability data and calculate adsorption capacities of GAC and IX for long and short chain PFAAs to evaluate treatment longevity and cost.

evidence_chunks.text: Another limitation of the existing studies is that the majority of the studies provides isotherm testing results without accounting for transport phenomena of PFAS in a fixed-bed adsorber, the predominant mode of operation in activated carbon adsorption.
More practical and applicable approaches, yet less precise, are to use a numerical simulation with isotherm data, or a rapid small-scale column test (RSSCT) based on a similitude approach.
McCleaf et al. conducted a pilot-scale GAC adsorber test with an empty bed contact time (EBCT) of 6.1 min for assessing the breakthrough of 14 PFAS spiked in groundwater.

evidence_chunks.text: Activated carbon (AC) adsorption continues to be the default technology to remove low levels of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from water, despite varying reports of the relatively early breakthrough of short-chain PFAS and high operating costs.
Ion-exchange processes using regenerable and single-use media have been emerging as practical alternatives which may provide improved treatment and system performance.

Treatability testing on PFAS-impacted groundwater using batch-equilibration reactors and column flushing apparatus experiments was implemented to compare removal efficiency, breakthrough, and longevity of various media, specifically for shorter chain PFAS.

evidence_chunks.text: The present Rapid Small-Scale Column Test study compares the removal of a suite of both long- and short-chain PFAS from groundwater.

The results show that re-agglomerated, bituminous coal-based GACs, whether virgin or reactivated, are capable of effectively removing long- and short-chain PFAS with four or more perfluorinated carbons.
Perfluorobutanoic acid, a perfluorinated carboxylic acid with just three perfluorinated carbons, reached breakthrough far more quickly than all other PFAS in this study.
